newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says security must come before aid to Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU says security must come before aid to Albania.

text.p: Military security must be ensured before humanitarian aid can be dispensed in Albania, European commissioner Emma Bonino said on Friday.

Stockpiles of aid, mostly in the form of medical supplies and flour from countries such as Serbia and Croatia, could be flown swiftly into the the balkan state provided the safety of relief workers was secured, she said.
"Humanitarian aid is ready and could be delivered in two or three days on the condition of security," Bonino told a news conference.

EU foreign ministers, scheduled to meet in Brussels on Monday, will be asked by the Commission to provide a blueprint for such security measures, Bonino said, adding she was confident that a solution could be found.
The EU commissioner stressed that time was of the essence if a major humanitarian rescue mission was to be avoided.
An EU fact-finding mission which visited Albania earlier this week will report its findings to the ministers on Monday.
It is estimated that $10 million in basic medical supplies and 10,000 tonnes of flour are urgently needed.
